terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the ticket here to see what the printer would get.

tasks.title: Print the party size
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `Tickets.java`, print one line that says how many people travel on the ticket, `adults` and `children` together:

```
Passengers: 5
```

Check runs your Task 1 lines with parties of its own and reads the number after `Passengers:`.
nextSteps: Print the line with the text and the two names joined by `+`.
Run `java Tickets.java`: is the number what you expected?
Read the part of the lesson about the order `+` works in.
Make Java add the two numbers before they join the text.
hints: Java reads a line of `+` from the left. Once the left side is a `String`, each `+` after it joins text.
Brackets are worked out first, so a sum inside brackets is added as numbers before it meets the text.

docs.title: String concatenation in the Java language

tasks.title: Make the short code
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, make a `String` called `code`: the first three letters of `destination`, in capital letters. For `Corran` that is `COR`.

Check runs your Task 2 lines with destinations of its own, one of exactly three letters, and reads `code`.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about positions in a `String`.
Cut the first three letters out of `destination` with `substring`.
Turn them into capitals with the method the lesson shows.
hints: Positions start at 0. The first three letters are at positions 0, 1 and 2.
`substring(start, end)` gives the letters from `start` up to, but not including, `end`. `toUpperCase()` gives a capital copy.
The line has the shape `String code = destination.substring(0, ...).toUpperCase();`.

tasks.title: Check the boat on the ticket
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, make a `boolean` called `rightBoat`: `true` when `ticketBoat` is the same text as `todayBoat`, `false` when it is not. `ticketBoat` is cut out of the ticket near the top of the file.

Check runs your Task 3 lines with tickets and boats of its own, some that match and some that do not, and reads `rightBoat`.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about comparing text.
Make `rightBoat` with the comparison it recommends.
Print it and run the program: today's ticket is for today's boat.
Change `todayBoat` at the top for a moment and run again, then change it back.
hints: Comparing two `String`s with `==` looks right and often says false for the same text. The lesson explains why.
Every `String` has a method that compares its letters with another `String`'s and gives `true` or `false`.
The line has the shape `boolean rightBoat = ticketBoat.equals(...);`.

tasks.title: Fit the ticket on the printer
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, the printer fits 24 characters on a line. Make an `int` called `spaceLeft`: how many characters are left on the line after `ticket`. Spaces count as characters.

Check runs your Task 4 lines with tickets of its own and reads `spaceLeft`.
nextSteps: Find the method that gives how many characters a `String` has.
Count the characters of today's ticket by hand to check the number.
hints: Every `String` knows its own length, spaces included.
`length()` is a method, so it needs its round brackets, even with nothing inside.
The line has the shape `int spaceLeft = 24 - ticket.length();`.
